rubric.description: Unable to perform task or operates unsafely.

rubric.label: Partially Demonstrated
rubric.description: Requires direct intervention; significant procedural errors.

rubric.label: With Support
rubric.description: Follows safety with occasional prompts; minor technique gaps.

rubric.label: Competent
rubric.description: Executes safely and accurately per trade standards.

rubric.label: Strongly Demonstrated
rubric.description: Exemplary speed, precision, and adherence to electrical safety.

competencies.name: Wiring and Cable Laying
competencies.title: Wiring and Cable Laying
competencies.description: Prepare, layout, and secure surface and concealed wiring conduits, cables, and connections per load calculations.
performanceCriteria: Select proper wire gauges (e.g. 1.5 sq mm for lighting, 4.0 sq mm for power) based on load specifications
Lay PVC/GI conduits accurately according to layout drawings without sharp bends
Follow standardized color-coding (Phase: Red/Brown, Neutral: Black/Blue, Earth: Green/Yellow)
Secure cables with saddles at standard intervals (< 30cm) and terminate in junction boxes
observableIndicators: Correct wire gauge chosen for application load
Conduit saddle spacing <= 30cm and neatly aligned
Proper stripping length without conductor nicking

assessmentChecklist.task: Selection of wire gauges and color coding
assessmentChecklist.criteria: Selected 1.5 sq mm for lighting and 4.0 sq mm for power circuits; followed Red-Phase, Black-Neutral, Green-Earth.
Conduit is aligned vertically and horizontally with saddles spaced no more than 30 cm apart.
Wires stripped without strand nicking and terminated with proper ferrules/lugs in junction box.

competencies.name: Installation of Distribution Board & Switchgear
competencies.title: Installation of Distribution Board & Switchgear
competencies.description: Mount, dress, and wire distribution boards, MCBs, RCCBs, and domestic switch accessories.
performanceCriteria: Mount distribution board plumb and level at the recommended ergonomic height (1.5m - 1.8m)
Install and wire MCB and 30mA RCCB correctly for shock and overcurrent protection
Connect single-pole switches on the live phase conductor only, never neutral
Dress wires neatly inside panel with spiral bands and provide proper circuit labeling
observableIndicators: Distribution board plumb and secure on wall
RCCB and MCB connected in proper line/load orientation
Switches switch live phase conductor only
requiredEvidence: Live video of MCB/RCCB trip testing

assessmentChecklist.criteria: DB mounted plumb and level; metal body bonded firmly to the earth terminal busbar.
Incoming phase connects to DP isolator/RCCB first, then loops to outgoing SP MCBs.
Phase wire is interrupted through the switch; neutral is looped directly to lamp/socket.

competencies.name: Earthing and Testing Procedures
competencies.title: Earthing and Testing Procedures
competencies.description: Construct, measure, and verify pipe/plate earthing and perform continuity and insulation resistance tests.
performanceCriteria: Verify pipe or plate earthing electrode installation with salt and charcoal layers
Perform earth resistance measurement with Earth Clamp / 3-point Megger (< 5 Ohms target)
Execute circuit continuity check between Phase and Neutral, and insulation test between Conductor and Earth
Verify polarity of all installed 3-pin 16A/6A power socket outlets
observableIndicators: Earth pit resistance verified < 5 ohms
Insulation resistance verified > 1 Megaohm
Socket right-pin is Live, top is Earth
requiredEvidence: Earth resistance reading on digital tester

assessmentChecklist.criteria: Meter leads connected correctly; verified earth pit resistance is below 5 Ohms.
Megger test between phase and earth shows resistance greater than 1 Megaohm.
Earth pin (top larger) connected to ground; right pin Live; left pin Neutral.

competencies.name: Health, Safety & Standard Operating Procedures
competencies.title: Health, Safety & Standard Operating Procedures
competencies.description: Implement Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), Lock-Out Tag-Out (LOTO), and electrical hazard prevention.
performanceCriteria: Wear standard 1000V rated insulated gloves, safety shoes, and eye protection
Verify circuit de-energization using calibrated neon tester or DMM prior to touching conductors
Implement Lock-Out Tag-Out (LOTO) procedures on main isolator switch during maintenance
Demonstrate correct response to electrical fire (CO2 / dry powder, never water) and victim rescue protocol
observableIndicators: PPE worn during live terminal proximity
Zero-voltage verified before touching terminals
LOTO lock and tag secured at isolator

assessmentChecklist.criteria: Candidate is wearing 1000V rated insulated rubber gloves and electrical safety boots.
Tested circuit with multimeter to confirm 0V before stripping or touching cables.
Applied safety padlock and tag to main breaker box during simulated maintenance.

competencies.name: Timber Marking, Sizing and Precision Cutting
competencies.title: Timber Marking, Sizing and Precision Cutting
competencies.description: Interpret fabrication sketches, mark reference lines with try-square, and execute rip, cross, and miter cuts accurately.
performanceCriteria: Measure and mark timber dimensions with try-square within 1mm accuracy
Select and operate appropriate hand saw or circular saw with suitable tooth count
Plane edges flat and square to true face using jack plane and check with winding sticks
Maintain cutting tool blade sharpness and clear work area of chips
observableIndicators: Measurement marks clear with knife/pencil and true square to edge
Squareness verified with combination square across faces
Cut line clean with minimal tear-out on finished side
requiredEvidence: Check of squareness against reference square

assessmentChecklist.criteria: Timber marked with try-square and ruler within 1mm tolerance from drawing.
Straight, clean cuts along marked line with no blade wander or kickback.
Edge planed flat, square (90 deg to face), and verified with try-square.

competencies.name: Woodworking Joinery and Assembly
competencies.title: Woodworking Joinery and Assembly
competencies.description: Fabricate mortise-and-tenon, halving, rebate, and dowel joints, and assemble structural components using adhesive and fasteners.
performanceCriteria: Chisel mortise pocket with clean walls and matching square shoulder tenon
Dry-fit joints to verify tight contact (< 0.5mm gap) before gluing
Apply PVA/polyurethane adhesive evenly and clamp securely with uniform pressure
Check diagonal squareness of frame assembly using tape measure
observableIndicators: Mortise and tenon fit snugly by hand pressure without excessive force
Equal diagonal measurements confirming squareness of frame
Glue squeeze-out cleaned neatly without grain discoloration
requiredEvidence: Glued and clamped frame assembly photos

assessmentChecklist.criteria: Tenon fits snugly into mortise with square shoulders touching flush.
Clamps applied squarely; diagonal measurements equal within 1.5mm.
Hinge mortise chiseled flush with timber surface without splitting.

competencies.name: Carpentry Workshop Health, Safety and Dust Control
competencies.title: Carpentry Workshop Health, Safety and Dust Control
competencies.description: Demonstrate safe power tool usage, dust mask and eye protection, push stick usage, and fire safety.
performanceCriteria: Wear eye protection goggles and N95 dust mask during cutting and routing
Use push sticks and featherboards when feeding material near spinning saw blades
Inspect blades and cords for damage prior to energizing power tools
Store flammable finishes and adhesives in designated ventilated safety cabinets
observableIndicators: Eye protection and dust mask worn continuously during tool operation
Push stick utilized on saw table when fingers are < 10cm from blade
Workpiece clamped firmly before drilling or routing
requiredEvidence: Push stick usage during cutting clip

assessmentChecklist.criteria: Wears safety glasses and dust mask during sawing, routing, and sanding.

assessmentChecklist.task: Power tool blade guarding and push stick
assessmentChecklist.criteria: Adjusts blade guard and uses push stick when cutting narrow boards.
Disconnects tool power before changing bits/blades; vacuums dust buildup.

rpl_qualification_packs.description: Installation, assembly, testing, and maintenance of CPVC/UPVC/GI water supply pipes, drainage traps, sanitary fixtures, and booster pumps.

rubric.label: Not Demonstrated
rubric.description: Leaks detected; incorrect pipe slope; unsafe tool use.

rubric.label: Partially Demonstrated

rubric.label: With Support
rubric.description: Pressure test passes after re-tightening; needs guidance on slope.

rubric.label: Competent
rubric.description: Zero leaks at 5 bar; correct gradient on waste pipe; clean solvent welds.

rubric.label: Strongly Demonstrated
rubric.description: Flawless alignment, pressure test hold for 30 mins, optimal hydraulic routing.

competencies.name: Cold & Hot Water Supply Pipeline Installation
competencies.title: Cold & Hot Water Supply Pipeline Installation
competencies.description: Cut, ream, join, and support CPVC, UPVC, and GI supply pipes with solvent cement and threaded fittings.
performanceCriteria: Cut pipes perpendicular to axis and remove internal and external burrs
Apply primer and solvent cement evenly to pipe and socket, rotate 90 deg and hold
Apply PTFE tape in direction of thread and tighten with pipe wrench without cracking fitting
Anchor horizontal and vertical pipelines with pipe clamps at recommended spans
observableIndicators: Square pipe cut without burrs or ridges
Uniform solvent ring around socket joint
Adequate pipe clamping support at correct pitch
requiredEvidence: Photos of pipe joints and solvent bead

assessmentChecklist.criteria: Cut is square; internal burr reamed cleanly to prevent flow restriction.
Solvent applied smoothly; joint held firmly for 30s; bead visible around circumference.
Tape applied clockwise 5-7 turns; threaded smoothly without cross-threading.

competencies.name: Drainage, Waste & Vent (DWV) System & Fixture Installation
competencies.title: Drainage, Waste & Vent (DWV) System & Fixture Installation
competencies.description: Layout sanitary drain pipes with proper gravitational slope, install P-traps, water closets, washbasins, and test for free flow.
performanceCriteria: Maintain minimum 1:40 (2.5%) gravitational slope on soil and waste lines
Install water seal traps (P-trap, S-trap, bottle trap) to prevent foul sewer gases
Mount sanitaryware level and plumb, secure with brass screws, and seal with silicone
Check free discharge and water trap seal retention under flow
observableIndicators: Drain slope verified with spirit level
Trap water seal >= 50mm preserved
Sanitaryware firmly bolted with anti-vibration washers
requiredEvidence: Spirit level on drain pipe photo

assessmentChecklist.criteria: Minimum 2% slope maintained towards gully or inspection chamber.
P-trap installed level with adequate water seal to block foul odors.
Washbasin mounted level; silicone bead applied neat along wall boundary.

competencies.name: Hydrostatic Pressure Testing & Safety Procedures
competencies.title: Hydrostatic Pressure Testing & Safety Procedures
competencies.description: Conduct hydrostatic leak testing at 5 bar pressure, follow trench safety, and handle hazardous sewer gases safely.
performanceCriteria: Fill pipeline with water, bleed air, and pressurize to 5 bar with hydraulic test pump
Hold pressure for 15-30 minutes and monitor pressure gauge for drops
Wear rubber safety boots, waterproof gloves, and eye protection in confined trenches
Safely ventilate confined drainage chambers prior to entry
observableIndicators: Pressure gauge holds steady without pressure loss
Waterproof PPE and safety gloves worn during testing
Immediate remedial action taken if joint weeping detected
requiredEvidence: Pressure gauge video at start and 15 mins

assessmentChecklist.criteria: Pressurized to 5 bar; zero drops observed on pressure gauge over 15 minutes.
Safety boots, gloves, and helmet worn during trench plumbing and testing.
Tools disinfected after waste line servicing; hands washed per sanitary protocol.

assessmentMethods: Live Engine Tappet / Brake Service Demonstration

rubric.label: Not Demonstrated
rubric.description: Incorrect fastener torque; stripped threads; unsafe bike support.

rubric.label: Partially Demonstrated
rubric.description: Follows manual with frequent errors; forgets safety checks (oil level, brake fluid).

rubric.label: With Support
rubric.description: Performs service correctly but requires supervision with feeler gauge or multimeter.

rubric.label: Competent
rubric.description: Sets valve clearance to spec (+/- 0.01mm); torques to spec; safe lift practice.

rubric.label: Strongly Demonstrated
rubric.description: Expert diagnostic speed, flawless procedure, clean workshop management.

competencies.name: Engine Servicing, Oil Change & Valve Clearance (Tappet) Tuning
competencies.title: Engine Servicing, Oil Change & Valve Clearance (Tappet) Tuning
competencies.description: Drain and replenish engine lubricant, clean/replace filters, inspect spark plug, and adjust valve lash to manufacturer specification using feeler gauge.
performanceCriteria: Drain warm engine oil into waste container, inspect for metal debris, and replace crush washer
Torque drain bolt to specified torque (typically 20-25 Nm) without over-tightening
Align TDC (Top Dead Center) timing mark on flywheel before measuring valve clearance
Use feeler gauge to measure intake and exhaust valve clearances and adjust locknut
observableIndicators: Engine aligned to TDC on compression stroke
Feeler gauge provides light drag when measuring clearance
New oil filled to specified level on dipstick
requiredEvidence: Feeler gauge valve lash measurement video

assessmentChecklist.criteria: Drained completely, drain plug torqued with new washer, oil level verified on dipstick.
Electrode condition evaluated; gap measured and set to 0.7-0.8mm with wire gauge.
Flywheel set to TDC; clearance adjusted to manufacturer spec (e.g. 0.08mm intake / 0.12mm exhaust).

competencies.name: Brake System Overhaul, Bleeding & Drive Chain Maintenance
competencies.title: Brake System Overhaul, Bleeding & Drive Chain Maintenance
competencies.description: Service hydraulic disc and mechanical drum brakes, bleed brake lines to eliminate air bubbles, inspect pad wear, and clean/lube/tension drive chain.
performanceCriteria: Measure brake pad and shoe lining thickness against service limit (> 1.5mm)
Bleed hydraulic brake line using DOT4 fluid until firm lever feel and zero bubbles
Inspect drive chain slack (20-30mm) and align rear wheel axle adjusters evenly
Lubricate chain with dedicated O-ring safe chain lube after degreasing
observableIndicators: Brake lever feels firm without sponginess
Zero air bubbles exiting bleed screw during pump cycle
Chain slack within 20-30mm and wheel spins freely without brake binding

assessmentChecklist.task: Brake pad inspection and disc cleaning
assessmentChecklist.criteria: Pads checked for even wear; disc rotor inspected for scoring/runout.
System bled completely; reservoir topped with fresh DOT4; firm lever action achieved.
Slack set to 25mm; axle nuts torqued; rear wheel alignment marks match on both swingarm sides.

competencies.name: Automotive Workshop Safety, Chemical Handling & Battery Protocol
competencies.title: Automotive Workshop Safety, Chemical Handling & Battery Protocol
competencies.description: Vehicle center-stand stability, handling sulfuric acid/electrolyte, waste oil disposal, and fire extinguisher readiness.
performanceCriteria: Support motorcycle stably on center-stand or hydraulic service ramp with wheel lock
Wear nitrile gloves and eye protection when handling solvent, oil, or battery acid
Dispose waste fluids in environmental recycling containers (never drain in soil)
Disconnect battery negative (-) terminal first before performing electrical work
observableIndicators: Motorcycle securely anchored during servicing
Nitrile gloves worn when handling oil and chemicals
Battery disconnected negative terminal first

assessmentChecklist.criteria: Bike placed securely on center-stand on flat, solid ground with wheel chock.
Disconnected ground (-) lead first to prevent accidental wrench shorting to frame.
Used oil and brake fluid stored in labeled containers for authorized disposal.

rpl_qualification_packs.jobRole: Welder - MMAW / Shielded Metal Arc Welding Specialist
rpl_qualification_packs.disclaimer: DEMO QUALIFICATION PACK for RPL simulation
rpl_qualification_packs.description: Preparing metal joints, selecting electrodes, setting welding current, and depositing sound fillet and groove welds on carbon steel in 1G, 2G, and 3G positions per welding procedure specifications (WPS).

rubric.label: Not Demonstrated
rubric.description: Lack of fusion; excessive undercut; arc strike outside joint; unsafe.

rubric.label: Partially Demonstrated
rubric.description: Inconsistent bead width; heavy spatter; incomplete penetration; slag inclusions.

rubric.label: With Support
rubric.description: Passes basic visual check with minor surface porosity; needs assistance setting current.

rubric.label: Competent
rubric.description: Uniform bead ripple; complete penetration; minimal undercut (< 0.5mm); slag peels cleanly.

rubric.label: Strongly Demonstrated
rubric.description: X-ray quality weld; impeccable root pass, zero porosity, perfect throat thickness.

competencies.name: Metal Preparation, Fit-Up and Machine Parameter Setting
competencies.title: Metal Preparation, Fit-Up and Machine Parameter Setting
competencies.description: Clean base metal, grind bevel angles (30-35 deg), fit up root face/gap (2-3mm), and adjust amperage according to electrode diameter.
performanceCriteria: Remove rust, scale, and grease from weld joint edges using angle grinder or wire brush
Prepare single-V bevel edge on plates > 6mm with 60 deg included angle
Tack weld plates with 2.5mm root gap to allow full root penetration
Select correct current (e.g. 90-110A for 3.15mm E6013 / E7018) for joint thickness
observableIndicators: Base metal ground bright and free of oxide
Uniform root gap maintained with spacer / tack welds
Amperage set within recommended electrode manufacturer range
requiredEvidence: Tacked joint photo with root gap shown

assessmentChecklist.criteria: Plates ground to bare metal 25mm on either side of joint; bevel uniform.
Tack welds small, sound, and root gap measured consistently at 2.5mm.
Chose correct electrode (e.g. E7018 for structural); amperage matched.

competencies.name: Welding Deposition, Bead Control & Slag Removal
competencies.title: Welding Deposition, Bead Control & Slag Removal
competencies.description: Maintain steady arc length, travel angle (15-20 deg), and travel speed to deposit uniform root, fill, and cap passes in fillet and butt joints.
performanceCriteria: Strike arc cleanly without stray arc strikes on adjacent base metal
Maintain arc length equal to electrode core diameter (approx 3mm)
Execute stringer or slight weaving bead with consistent travel speed
Chip slag completely between passes and inspect for inter-pass defects
observableIndicators: Smooth arc sound (steady crackle, no sputtering)
Uniform bead width and ripple pattern
Slag removed completely before subsequent passes
requiredEvidence: Cross-section or fillet break test photo

assessmentChecklist.criteria: Arc initiated smoothly inside joint; drag angle maintained at 15-20 degrees.
Bead width consistent (+/- 1mm); flat to slight convex reinforcement.
Slag removed with chipping hammer and wire brush; no trapped slag in toes.

competencies.name: Welding Safety, Eye Protection & Fume Extraction
competencies.title: Welding Safety, Eye Protection & Fume Extraction
competencies.description: Protect against arc radiation (UV/IR), electrical shock in damp areas, fume inhalation, and hot metal burns.
performanceCriteria: Use approved auto-darkening helmet with shade DIN 10-12 and flame-retardant leather apron and spats
Wear heavy-duty split leather welding gauntlets at all times during welding
Ensure welding earth clamp is attached directly to workpiece near weld zone
Work in well-ventilated area or utilize portable fume extraction hood
observableIndicators: Welding helmet shade active prior to arc ignition
Full leather PPE (gloves, apron, spats) in place
Earth clamp firmly clamped to clean metal

assessmentChecklist.criteria: Uses helmet with correct shade; warns nearby personnel before striking arc.
Wearing leather gauntlets, protective leather jacket/apron and safety boots.
Clears flammable materials within 10 meters; works under fume ventilation.

rubric.label: Partially Demonstrated
